title: Construct a Taro Linkage Map Using Onemap
author: Michael Kantar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.85xhy7n

steps.title: Install onemap (Option 1)
steps.instruction: Download and install Rtools from https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools, verify with find_rtools(debug = TRUE), then install devtools (install.packages("devtools")), load it (library(devtools)), install onemap from GitHub (devtools::install_github("Cristianetaniguti/onemap")), and load onemap (library("onemap")).

steps.title: Install onemap (Option 2)
steps.instruction: If using R 5.6, install the CRAN version (install.packages(onemap)), load it (library(onemap)), then install and load vcfR (install.packages("vcfR"); library("vcfR")).

steps.title: Set working directory
steps.instruction: Set the R working directory to your project folder (setwd("/your/working/directory/"))

steps.title: Convert VCF to onemap format
steps.instruction: Ensure the VCF filename has no trailing .txt, read the VCF (vcfR.object <- read.vcfR("imputed_loci_06052019.vcf")), then convert it to onemap format with parent files (example_out <- onemap_read_vcfR(vcfR.object = vcfR.object, parent1 = "P230.sam.mapped.bam", parent2 = "P255.sam.mapped.bam", cross = "outcross")).

steps.title: Inspect marker genotypes
steps.instruction: Plot the dataset (plot(example_out)) and plot the number of markers by segregation type (plot_by_segreg_type(example_out)).

steps.title: Identify redundant markers
steps.instruction: Find redundant marker bins (bins <- find_bins(example_out, exact = FALSE)) and display them (bins).

steps.title: Create dataset without redundancy
steps.instruction: Create a new onemap object excluding redundant markers (bins_example <- create_data_bins(example_out, bins)) and display it (bins_example).

steps.title: Test segregation patterns
steps.instruction: Run segregation tests (segreg_test <- test_segregation(bins_example)) and print the results (print(segreg_test)).

steps.title: Identify distorted markers
steps.instruction: List marker names with distortion (select_segreg(segreg_test, distorted = TRUE)), obtain their numbers (dist <- select_segreg(segreg_test, distorted = TRUE, numbers = TRUE)), obtain numbers without distortion (no_dist <- select_segreg(segreg_test, distorted = FALSE, numbers = TRUE)) and display the non‑distorted list (no_dist).

steps.title: Determine suggested LOD
steps.instruction: Calculate a suggested LOD score (LOD_sug <- suggest_lod(bins_example)) and display it (LOD_sug).

steps.title: Compute two‑point recombination
steps.instruction: Estimate two‑point recombination fractions with the suggested LOD and max.rf = 0.3 (twopts <- rf_2pts(bins_example, LOD = LOD_sug, max.rf = 0.3)) and display the object (twopts).

steps.title: Create marker sequences without distortion
steps.instruction: Generate sequences using only non‑distorted markers (mark_no_dist <- make_seq(twopts, c(no_dist))).

steps.title: Group markers into linkage groups
steps.instruction: Group markers into linkage groups with the same LOD and max.rf (lg <- group(mark_no_dist, LOD = LOD_sug, max.rf = 0.3)) and print a summary (print(lg, detailed = FALSE)).

steps.title: Build genetic maps
steps.instruction: Initialize a list for maps (maps <- vector("list", lg$n.groups)); for each group i (i from 1 to lg$n.groups) create an ordered sequence (maps[[i]] <- make_seq(order_seq(input.seq = make_seq(lg, i), twopt.alg = "rcd"), "force")).

steps.title: Visualize maps
steps.instruction: Draw the maps with markers unlabeled (draw_map(maps, names = FALSE, grid = TRUE, cex.mrk = 0.7)) and export a PNG image (draw_map2(maps, output = "maps.png")).

steps.title: Export map to file
steps.instruction: Define the output filename (file.out <- "map_LOD=5.97,max.rf=0.3.csv") and write the first map to it (write_map(map1, file.out)).
